## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the

This PR adds foundation for Blueprints to scripts. 

Adding Blueprint support for scripts, feels like a sensible next step. It allows users to share their scripts (using imports). Additionally, Blueprint provides inputs, which can be used to set script defaults.

Together with the addition of Selectors for script fields in 2021.4.0, can lift the scripts more friendly level.

This is a future mockup:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/195327/113406358-a3b26400-93ab-11eb-9a99-d7da0bfeb52e.png)


This will work with this PR:

```yaml
# scripts.yaml
confirm:
  alias: Confirm the action
  use_blueprint:
    path: homeassistant/confirmable_notification.yaml
    input:
      notify_device: 12343242
      title: "Open the garage door?"
      message: "Detected you are close, open the garage door?"
      confirm_action:
        - service: cover.open
          target:
            entity_id: cover.garage_door
```

The example Blueprint used above is in this PR.

TODO:
- [x] Cleanup
- [x] Tests for multi domain support
- [x] Tests for the blueprints
- [x] Fix all breaking "other" tests cases
- [x] Add Blueprint inputs in the trace

Other:
- [ ] Frontend. The first screenshot works, but not really. Need some frontend peeps for that 😬 

## Additional note

As a side effect of this logic, scripts can now be used in split configuration scenarios better (e.g., let the UI write to `scripts.yaml` while having your manual ones in a different location). This is the same logic as in automations.

```yaml
# configuration.yaml
script: !include scripts.yaml
scripts manual: !include_dir_merge_named ./scripts
```

Closes #38456.

issue_context.title: Including scripts.yaml and a folder with scripts at the same time is not possible (legacy scripts and GUI editor co-existing way)
issue_context.body:
**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
All versions up to current 0.114.0.dev20200731

**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**
Never worked so far

**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**
Docker on arm based SBC

**Component/platform:**
https://www.home-assistant.io/components/script/

**Description of problem:**
This does not work. The second line does not do anything.
```
script: !include scripts.yaml
script manual: !include_dir_merge_named scripts
```

Please refer this two years old, stale and closed issue for the further detail. Very well described.
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/15628


**Additional information:**
No debug logs. because HA does not shows anything in the log about loading scripts.

**Additional comment:**
First, it has been like this for years, so feels like a feature we live with.
Please note that, the HA documentation actually **_does not_** mention Automations and Scripts would work like above.
```
you can, however, have multiple top-level !includes for a given integration, if you give a different label to each one:
```
And the given an example,
```
light:
- platform: group
  name: Bedside Lights
  entities:
    - light.left_bedside_light
    - light.right_bedside_light

# define more light groups in a separate file
light groups: !include light-groups.yaml

# define some light switch mappings in a different file
light switches: !include light-switches.yaml
```
I guess one can argue automation and scripts are not **'integration'**, but **'core component'**.
Of course, then this does not explain why bellow works great for years. Both lines a executed and loaded.
```
automation: !include automations.yaml
automation manual: !include_dir_merge_list automations
```

Anyway and unfortunately this hasn't been fixed for over two years to my  knowledge.

Maybe there is nothing to fix, because it's just misunderstanding of the documentation. Maybe. 
One thing for sure is that the current situation and the unclear documentation has created fair amount of confusions over the period.

Note that a member tried to clarify this in the documentation, 
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/14084/commits/31119773ae497ecae8bb6be5dabd589c2a27df5b

but, apparently met an opposition,
>> Actually this note is incorrect. It does work, and have used it myself as well.
>>...
>>I will not allow for documenting bugs in our documentation.
_Originally posted by @frenck in https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/14084#issuecomment-667494369_





Meanwhile, I tried to get some information from my past configurations and logs over the years, but could not find any error logs or any HA version that worked as @frenck mentioned, or anything useful. And could not find any official documentation that it would work, but a few community posts it would. (and posts that it wouldn't)

At the moment, I am not really sure that this is a bug or intended feature or misunderstanding of unclear phrase, but has been asked to just raise an issue of it.

>>I'm sorry, for the fourth time now, would you please just raise an issue?
_Originally posted by @frenck in https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/14084#issuecomment-667524482_

So with much lack of useful information produced by myself and all that I could gather, this is it.
I am especially sorry for the lack of useful information, at least identifying HA version that works would speed up the things.

One more thing, there is a related work-around worth mentioning 
https://community.home-assistant.io/t/script-editor-and-split-up-files/40459/20?u=grashugger

As this work-around works rock solid for both legacy scripts management and new GUI editor.

Ok, so a bit further in, this requires some significant rewrites to how we load and process YAML.
My current estimation is this needs 1 or 2 days of work (or more). The duration of this is mainly caused by the high risk of making changes here (which require care and tests).

This functionality of loading the same platform using multiple configurations was introduced 6 years ago and was aimed at platforms. #16177 introduced this to packages in 2018. We are currently moving away from platforms in general now ADR-0007 in place.

Furthermore, this logic currently only applies to lists and is handled by the individual integrations. For example:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c403c77cff0ea684027bf99f472e4fab5a52d34d/homeassistant/components/automation/__init__.py#L535

For which the following helper is used, which takes care of the domain configured with different labels:

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c403c77cff0ea684027bf99f472e4fab5a52d34d/homeassistant/helpers/__init__.py#L35-L41

Entity components also handle this (e.g., light, switch, fan, ...)

### First Proposal (1-2 days)

- In either [`load_yaml_config_file`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c403c77cff0ea684027bf99f472e4fab5a52d34d/homeassistant/config.py#L317-L337) or in [`async_hass_config_yaml`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c403c77cff0ea684027bf99f472e4fab5a52d34d/homeassistant/config.py#L302-L314) we process the configuration to merge these occurrences into a single domain key.
- In [`merge_packages_config`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c403c77cff0ea684027bf99f472e4fab5a52d34d/homeassistant/config.py#L654-L717), we will merge these labeled occurrences directly into the top-level single domain key as well.
- In [`merge_packages_config`](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c403c77cff0ea684027bf99f472e4fab5a52d34d/homeassistant/config.py#L654-L717), we merge items in the dictionary, but won't allow overwrites/duplicates to disallow collisions/surprises (as we already do).
- Remove the `config_per_platform` and `extract_domain_configs` helpers from `helpers/__init__.py`
- Remove the use of the `extract_domain_configs`/`config_per_platform` from all platforms that are currently implement logic to handle these cases:
  - `frontend`
  - `lovelace`
  - `automation`
  - `device_tracker`
  - `scene`
  - `mailbox`
  - `notify`
  - `onvif`
  - `sst`
  - `tts`
- Remove the use of the `config_per_platform` from the entity component platform setup logic

Doing this would make this feature work transparent across the whole of Home Assistant, and does not require any specific implementation on component or integration level. It will fix split configuration, e.g., groups and scripts as well.

Honestly, at this point, while it sounds cool, it makes things more consistent across the board and throws out quite a bit of logic from our codebase; It made me wonder if we should do this at all.

The biggest downside is to allow more "magic" in our configuration. While I'm a heavy user of configuration splitting, I'm not quite sure if this is splitting with an additional label is a good practice we should pursue for the future. Since this proposal would extend that... I'm not sure.

### Secondary Proposal (hotfix)

As a more secondary proposal, which is less intrusive, but also incomplete in solving the whole problem:

- Add the `config_per_platform`/`extract_domain_configs` helpers to the scripts component so it works
- Add handling to `merge_packages_config` to prevent silent overwrite (which caused examples presented in this issue to not cause any warnings or errors).

### Third proposal (months?)

All of these issues are actually caused by the UI. The UI writes to fixed files (e.g., `scripts.yaml` and `automations.yaml`. The need for adding a component to the configuration twice (with a label), is actually caused by having both a split configuration AND a working UI editor.

Ideally, those components should be using storage collections, in which the UI will write to the storage. This would remove the need for these weird configs to being with.

review_comments:
This is different logic than before. Previously we would only accept configuration under `script:` and not `script bla:` etc. 

Also, scripts do not have platforms, so using the platform helper seems odd.

This is what automations use at this point as well. I agree the helper name is weird, happy to address that in general in a follow-up PR (as it would affect around 30 uses in 16 files, unrelated to this PR).

The reason this is added is to make split config work and allows for splitting manual configuration from the `scripts.yaml` file which the UI uses to write to.

This mimicks the current behavior of automations, this would become more important as soon as a UI around these is created as well.
